You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: aria-hidden is put on the slot element of a slotted target, hiding the target itself.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [minor] The diff walks shadow roots with its own recursion and `document.createTreeWalker`, not the `ShadowTreeWalker` helper that FEATURE_FLOW names as the convention. Not reproduced as a bug.
- [minor] `shouldUseInert` inside shadow roots is untested and unexercisable here: jsdom has no `'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype`, so `supportsInert` is false and the option is silently ignored. My probe got `inert === undefined`. Not reproduced; the criterion's inert variant is unverified.
- [minor] An added wrapper div containing a `data-live-announcer` child stays visible (its non-announcer siblings are hidden). Identical in the light-DOM path, so this is pre-existing parity, not a shadow regression.
- [minor] A new host with a new shadow root attached to body after the call is hidden as a whole (`host aria-hidden=true`). The light-DOM equivalent is the same wholesale hide, so this is parity.
- [minor] `root as Element` / `acceptNode(root as Element)` casts added to make the `Element | ShadowRoot` walk type-check. Style only.
- [minor] Not reproduced: `[...visibleNodes].some(...)` runs for every shadow host in the walk, which is O(hosts × targets). No timing probe run.

Reply exactly:
{"found": "yes"|"no", "review": <review number or null>, "finding_quote": "<verbatim quote of the finding, or empty>",
